blocks.s: Augustine further distinguishes three kinds of vision: corporeal vision, by which we see with the bodily eyes things that are present to the senses; imaginary or imaginative vision, by which we see images and likenesses of things even when those things are absent from the bodily senses; and intellectual vision, by which the mind sees truth itself and the intelligible realities that have no corporeal form and can receive no image. The highest contemplation belongs to intellectual vision, and in its summit it reaches toward the vision of God himself, insofar as this is granted to a soul in the present state.
